title: The Surface of the Earth and Fossils
seo_title: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: The Surface of the Earth and Fossils Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Planet Earth; the surface of the Earth; sedimentary rock; fossils
standard_text: The Earth's surface is made of rock and soil. Weathering breaks rock into small pieces, which are carried away and deposited in layers that harden into sedimentary rock. Fossils are the remains or traces of plants and animals that lived long ago, preserved in rock; South Africa has important fossil sites. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 5, Planet Earth and Beyond: Planet Earth; the surface of the Earth; sedimentary rock; fossils)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): rocks and soil, weathering and erosion, sedimentary rock, how fossils form and South African fossils. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sediment.
key_sub: Fossils are found mostly in sedimentary rock.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has a thin outer layer called the crust, made of rock. Wind, water and temperature changes break rocks into small pieces (weathering). Soil is a mixture of tiny rock pieces, humus (rotting plants and animals), air and water.

Rivers carry sand and mud and drop them in layers. Over millions of years the layers are pressed and cemented into sedimentary rock, such as sandstone and shale. When a dead plant or animal is buried in sediment, it can become a fossil. The Karoo has many fossils of ancient reptiles, and the Cradle of Humankind has fossils of early humans.

Example

In undisturbed rock layers, which layer is the oldest?

Layers pile up over time.

Answer: the bottom layer

Example

Which kind of rock usually contains fossils?

It forms in layers.

Answer: sedimentary rock

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fossils form quickly.
  • Thinking soil is just broken rock.
  • Thinking fossils are found in lava rock.

items.q: How does a fossil form? This happens: “The soft parts rot away, leaving bones or shell.” What happens next?
c: Millions of years later, the rock wears away and the fossil is found.
Minerals slowly replace the bones, turning them to stone.
An animal dies and sinks to the bottom of a sea or lake.
More layers build up and press the sediment into rock.
items.e: Order: dies → covered → soft parts rot → layers press → minerals replace → found.

items.q: Is a fossilised fish skeleton a body fossil or a trace fossil?
items.e: Body fossils are parts of the living thing; trace fossils are signs it left behind, such as footprints.
